subject: Order schedule pricing: floor smoothing & spike-credit redline
messages:
From: Sarah Miller <sarah@brightwell.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 5 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing schedule questions + legal redlines

Hi Elliot,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. Our procurement and legal teams reviewed the draft order schedule and flagged two items that need clarification before we can route for signature: (1) the minimum monthly floor language in Exhibit C that effectively creates a hard floor for the first 12 months; (2) a mechanism for handling unexpected spikes in usage during onboarding that could otherwise trigger outsized true-ups.

Attached is Brightwell_OrderSchedule_v3.pdf with inline comments from our counsel (Brightwell Legal). High level asks: can you (a) soften the hard floor to an averaged-commitment approach (we suggested averaging over a quarter) and (b) add a short-term spike credit / onboarding buffer so we are not penalized for legitimate, short-lived bursts tied to migration/testing?

If you need an internal point from our side, include me and Ryan Chen from Legal (ryan@brightwell.com). Wed like to keep this targetable so we can close by the end of next week.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Miller
Head of Procurement, Brightwell Health

Attachment: Brightwell_OrderSchedule_v3.pdf (annotated)
From: Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Miller <sarah@brightwell.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 6 Sep 2026 10:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing schedule questions + legal redlines

Sarah 
Appreciate the detailed notes and the annotated schedule. Short answer: were willing to amend the floor mechanics and add an onboarding buffer, but we need concrete guardrails so the relief is objective and bounded. Proposed commercial compromise (high level):

- Floor smoothing: compute the minimum commitment as the greater of (i) 80% of quarterly average usage or (ii) the existing monthly floor, but measured as a rolling 3-month average rather than single-month snapshots. This prevents a one-off month from permanently setting an elevated floor.

- Onboarding/spike credit: a one-time "spike credit" equal to 10% of the first three months' committed spend applied as a credit against true-ups; any credits beyond that require prior written approval from Redwood finance.

Ive drafted suggested amendment text and attached it as proposed-amend-text.docx for your counsel to review. If Brightwell can accept the credit cap and rolling average, we can proceed and Ill have legal prepare a redline to Exhibit C.

If thats too constraining, tell me what threshold Brightwell needs and Ill run it with Neha and Karthik. Aim: keep this structured so we avoid open-ended concessions.

Best,
Elliot Price
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Office: 415-555-0123 | Mobile: 415-555-0199

Attachments: proposed-amend-text.docx
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Sep 2026 14:01:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Pricing schedule questions + legal redlines -- internal redline notes

Elliot / Karthik,

Forwarding Brightwells note and Elliots proposed compromise. High-level legal takeaways after a quick pass (see attached redline-exhibitC.docx):

- Definition clarity: we must narrow "Committed Spend" so it excludes charges expressly listed as pass-throughs (third-party infra credits) and one-off professional services line items. Otherwise the rolling-average calculation can be gamed.

- Spike credit cap: 10% for three months feels generous; suggest cap at 25% of one monthly invoice (not cumulative) to protect revenue. Alternatively, keep Elliots 10% but limit to the first 2 months only.

- Sunset & audit rights: add an explicit sunset for the spike credit (e.g., expires after first 90 days) and retain audit rights for Redwood to validate usage growth is not anomalous.

Ive inserted tracked changes into Exhibit C. Key edits are: tightened the definition of "Usage Baseline"; added an explicit cap on credit issuance; added a 90-day sunset; and a clause granting Redwood the right to decline credits if suspicious patterning is detected.

If you want the faster close, Id accept Elliots 10%/3-month proposal only if Brightwell agrees to the narrower Committed Spend definition and the 90-day sunset. Otherwise push for the 25%/1-month cap.

- Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redline-exhibitC.docx
From: Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Miller <sarah@brightwell.com>, Ryan Chen <ryan@brightwell.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing schedule questions + legal redlines

Sarah / Ryan,

Thanks for the annotated schedule and for looping counsel in. Quick update after internal review: we can accept a smoothing approach and an onboarding buffer with two clarifications from our legal team (Neha):

1) Spike credit: 10% credit applied to the first two months invoices (not three) and capped at a single-month invoice amount (this is intended to be a limited operational buffer, not a recurring concession).

2) Committed Spend definition: we will adopt the rolling 3-month average for floor measurement, but Committed Spend will explicitly exclude pass-through third-party costs and discrete professional services line items.

Neha has redlined Exhibit C (attached) and were happy to share that redline in-track or produce a clean amendment. If Brightwell can confirm accept/counter on the two clarifications above, Ill share a DocuSign link for the order schedule and route to legal for final signatures. Proposed next steps:

- Brightwell to confirm accept/counter of the 10%/2-month spike credit and the Committed Spend exclusion language by EOD Thu 9 Sep.
- On acceptance, Redwood will upload a final amendment and send DocuSign (target signature by 10 Sep).

DocuSign preview: https://www.docusign.com/preview/DOC-987654 — note this is a live envelope placeholder; the final will reference deal DW-2026-0791.

If you prefer a short call to resolve quickly, Im available Wed 8/9am PT.

Thanks,
Elliot
